text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To understand your infant's recurrent stridor and wheezing, please describe exactly what activities trigger these symptoms, such as feeding, crying, or lying down. Additionally, have you noticed any difficulty breathing or feeding issues?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia with concurrent gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).

The symptoms of stridor worsening with neck flexion and crying, combined with post-prandial vomiting in an infant, are classic for laryngomalacia complicated by reflux. I will now request a neck flexion X-ray to confirm the anatomical findings. REQUEST IMAGES: Laryngomalacia_neck_flexion_Xray
